content:
OpenAI pioneered a system where product managers ship over 100,000 lines of code by leveraging AI agents guided by strict engineering-enforced guardrails. Engineers no longer write production code but instead build a "harness" that ensures AI-generated code is safe, scalable, and error-free.

• Engineers are banned from writing production code, focusing entirely on building the harness—comprising tests, documentation, and guardrails—to prevent AI mistakes before they happen.  
• A PM can write a PRD on Monday and ship a working pull request by Friday without any engineer touching the code, after an initial slow ramp-up period.  
• The harness consolidates tribal knowledge into a centralized prompt catalog, converts every failed AI run into permanent rules, and treats prompts like code with reviews and regression tests.  
• With 250,000 lines of markdown under version control, the system enables PMs, designers, and ops to contribute directly while engineers shift to building leverage and systemic quality.
